heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
translated_text:
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

REGENT OF MAGETAN

PROVINCE OF EAST JAVA

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGETAN REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definition of Terms

heading: Article 1
translated_text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Magetan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Magetan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magetan.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
7. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
8. Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
9. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
10. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Accompaniment is activities and actions carried out by companions to women and child victims of violence during the service and empowerment process.
14. Counseling is the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim and/or perpetrator increases in solving the problems faced;
15. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the Region that carry out integrated service functions for women and child victims of crime and/or violence, including as a center for information on women's empowerment and child protection.
16. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is one form of UPT established by the Regional Government that functions as an information center, service center and empowerment center for women and children. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children.
18. Household is family members and relatives including grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and non-relatives including domestic helpers and drivers who live and eat from 1 (one) kitchen and reside in 1 (one) house.

heading: Part Two
Article 3
CHAPTER II
CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

RESPONSIBILITY

Article 5

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is a shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. community;
c. family; and
d. parents.

heading: Article 6
Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

The responsibility of the community as referred to in Article 5 letter b is implemented in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children; and
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties.

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

Family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

Forms of empowerment of women victims of violence include:
a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and/or joint business groups; and
c. capital assistance.

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

Job training as referred to in Article 13 letter a includes:
a. skills training;
b. field work practice; and
c. apprenticeship.

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

Productive economic enterprises and/or joint business groups as referred to in Article 23 letter b include:
a. entrepreneurial skills training;
b. facilitation of the formation of joint business groups; and
c. business implementation assistance.

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

Capital assistance as referred to in Article 13 letter c includes:
a. work facilities and infrastructure assistance; and
b. facilitation of working capital assistance.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Fulfillment of the Rights of Child Victims of Violence

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

The Regional Government, UPT and the community are obliged to fulfill the rights of child victims of violence. The form of fulfillment of the rights of child victims of violence (2) as referred to in paragraph (1) is the fulfillment of the basic rights of children according to their needs.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

UPT/P2TP2A

heading: Part One
translated_text:
Part One

Article 18

1. The implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence is realized, among others, through the establishment of an integrated, one-stop and networked UPT established by the government, Regional Government, community, non-governmental organizations, donor institutions or other institutions.
2. UPT as referred to in paragraph (l) is P2TP2A (2) or similar institutions that have the same functions and roles.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

P2TP2A

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Establishment

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. P2TP2A is established in the Region.
2. The institutional structure of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is determined by Regent's Decree.
3. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (l) is under the coordination of the Regional Work Unit or other units handling women's empowerment and child protection.
4. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) does not have authority in the formulation of policies related to women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Coordination Mechanism

heading: Article 2O
translated_text:
Article 2O

1. The implementation of P2TP2A functions as referred to in Article 19, is carried out through coordination with the head of regional work units or other units handling women's empowerment and child protection.
2. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (l) is carried out in the form of:
a. coordination meetings with work networks;
b. consultation;
c. submission of data and information; and/or
d. follow-up on case handling.

heading: CHAPTER VI
CHAPTER llII
CHAPTER VHI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VHI

MONITORING AND REPORTING

Article 23

1. Monitoring of the implementation of protection of women and child victims of violence is carried out periodically and in an integrated manner every 6 (six) months by the regional apparatus organization that administers affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
2. Reporting on the implementation of protection of women and child victims of violence is carried out I (one) time per year and is coordinated by the regional apparatus organization that administers affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 24

1. Funding for the implementation of protection of women and child victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. other non-binding funding sources based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Budget management for the implementation of protection of victims of violence is carried out with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 25

P2TP2A as referred to in Article 19 shall be established no later than l (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

This Regional Regulation shall come into force upon promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Magetan Regency.

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGETAN REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGETAN REGENCY

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2016 CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGETAN REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore women and children need to be protected in their dignity and honor and their right to life must be guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Violence against women and children not only causes physical impacts but also psychological impacts which in general can affect the quality of life of women and children victims of violence.

On a national scale, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women). In addition, the Government has also enacted Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606) and Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419).
Furthermore, based on Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as most recently amended several times by Law Number 9 of 2015, women's empowerment and child protection constitute governmental affairs that must be implemented by Regional Governments.

As occurs in various regions, including Magetan Regency, there is currently a phenomenon of increasing acts of violence against women and children. To address this matter, regional regulations are needed that provide a basis for Regional Government and/or the community in realizing protection, so that victims are prevented and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Magetan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Therefore, policies are needed that can guarantee protection to free them from acts of violence, as well as improve their quality of life. Based on the considerations mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Magetan Regency concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article I

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGETAN REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by "respect for and fulfillment of the rights of victims" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of the basic rights of victims.

Letter b
What is meant by "justice" and gender equality is a condition where women are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access, as well as welfare.

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d
What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Regional Government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so that the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Letter e
Sufficiently clear.

heading: Article 3
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGETAN REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 3

Sufficiently clear.

heading: Article 4
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGETAN REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 4

Letter a
Physical violence referred to is caused by acts that result in pain, illness, or serious injury and or result in injury, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Forms of physical violence include slapping, hitting, spitting on, pulling hair/yanking, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons.

Letter b
Psychological violence referred to is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Forms of psychological violence include emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or degrading self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or frightening as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c
Sexual violence referred to is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect referred to is caused by:
a. acts that result in the non-fulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
c. acts of neglecting a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
d. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Exploitation referred to is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter f
Other violence referred to is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/or
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

heading: Article 12
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGETAN REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 12

Letter a Complaint, consultation, and counseling services include:
a. identification or initial recording of victims; and
b. informed consent, namely medical action consent given by the victim or their closest family after receiving a complete explanation regarding the medical action to be performed on the victim.

Letter b Accompaniment services include:
a. accompanying victims during the examination and health recovery process;
b. accompanying victims during the medicolegal process, namely medical services to provide optimal professional assistance in utilizing medical science for the purposes of law enforcement and justice. Medicolegal services include among others: visum et repertum and visum et psychiatricum;
c. accompanying victims during the examination process at the police, prosecutor's office and court;
d. monitoring the interests and rights of victims in the examination process at the police, prosecutor's office and court;
e. maintaining the privacy and confidentiality of victims from all parties who have no interest, including coverage by mass media;
f. coordinating with other companions; and g. providing continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.

Letter c Health services include:
a. first aid to victims;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and
c. referral to health services.

Letter d
Social rehabilitation services are services provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims.

Forms of social rehabilitation services through the provision of safe houses and social support.

Social support is carried out through:
a. spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.

Safe House (Shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.

Letter e Legal services to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding victims' rights and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and court hearing examination levels and helping victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Letter f
Social reintegration services aim to return victims to their families and social environment.

Social reintegration services are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. District/City Governments within one Regional area of East Java Province;
b. related agencies and institutions both government and non-government; and
c. village community institutions and/or local community leaders.

Letter g
Economic independence services through providing economic access are given to victims of violence, especially women victims of violence so they can be independent in running and maintaining their lives. Such economic services can be carried out by providing training that is appropriate to the skills or talents possessed by victims, so that victims can develop the skills or talents they possess when victims return to community life. In addition, PPT can provide business information as well as job vacancies related to the skills or abilities possessed by victims of violence.
